summary: Players lay tiles to build an ever-growing, layered city, choosing whether to place tiles for immediate resources or points, or stack them atop existing tiles to expand their influence and score at game's end. It's a light-to-medium tile-laying game with a clever 'card as tile, tile as card' resource loop and neat area-influence scoring.
praised: elegant, tactile layering mechanic where tiles double as cards
quick to teach and plays fast
good tension between short-term resources and long-term influence
criticised: can feel a bit dry or abstract thematically
limited direct interaction beyond spatial competition
less depth than other Georges/heavier euros for veteran gamers

interaction.kind: spatial competition for adjacency and territory influence

scoring.why: points come from building height, district influence, and resource-card sets, rewarding whoever balances expansion with efficient tile use
